title: What Is FNF? Friday Night Funkin' Explained for Players and Creators
summary: FNF is Friday Night Funkin', a free rhythm game where you match arrows to the beat. Here's how it works, where it came from, and what creators can learn.
body_markdown:
FNF stands for Friday Night Funkin', a rhythm game where you press arrow keys or tap arrows in time with the music. You play as Boyfriend, who takes on a series of opponents in musical face-offs to impress his girlfriend. It started as a free game jam project in 2020 and grew into one of the best-known indie rhythm games, with a large community of fan-made mods.


## What does FNF mean?


FNF is short for **Friday Night Funkin'** . Players use "FNF" for the game itself, and also for the huge range of fan-made versions, called mods, that add new characters and songs.


## How FNF works


Each song is a musical battle between Boyfriend and an opponent. During the song:


1. Arrows scroll up the screen toward four fixed targets: left, down, up, and right.
2. When an arrow reaches its target, you press the matching direction.
3. Accurate timing earns points and keeps your health bar up. Missed notes push the health bar toward your opponent.
4. If the health bar runs out, you lose the song and can try again.


Songs are grouped into **weeks** . Each week features one opponent and a few songs that get harder as you go. In Story Mode you play the weeks in order, and in Freeplay you pick any song you've reached.


## Who made Friday Night Funkin'?


FNF was created for the Ludum Dare 47 game jam in October 2020. The core team was programmer ninjamuffin99, artists PhantomArcade and evilsk8r, and composer Kawai Sprite. The game was released for free, and you can play it on[Newgrounds](https://www.newgrounds.com/portal/view/770371) or download it from[itch.io](https://ninja-muffin24.itch.io/funkin) .


Want to know more about the music? See[who composed the Friday Night Funkin' songs](https://www.hyperpad.com/blog/about-friday-night-funkin-composers) .


## Can you play FNF on iPhone or iPad?


Yes. The Funkin' Crew released[Friday Night Funkin' Mobile](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/friday-night-funkin-mobile/id6740428530) on the App Store in July 2025. It's free with ads and rated 13+. The original game still runs in a web browser on Newgrounds and as a download for computers.


If you'd rather make a game in the same style, see[how to make your own FNF mod on iOS](https://www.hyperpad.com/blog/fnf-mobile-on-ios) .


## Is FNF OK for kids?


That depends on the version and the child. Some fan-made mods include mature themes. The[parent's guide to Friday Night Funkin'](https://www.hyperpad.com/blog/fnf-kids) covers what to look for.


## Why FNF matters to game creators


FNF is a useful game to study because its design is so clear. Every part has one job:


- **The arrows** tell the player what to press.
- **The targets** show when to press it.
- **The music** sets the pace and difficulty.
- **The characters** react to how well the player is doing.


For a first rhythm prototype of your own, you only need four direction targets, notes that move toward them, touch controls, a timing window, a score and miss counter, and one short music loop. Build that version before you add characters, dialogue, menus, or several songs.


## Build an original rhythm game on iPad


You can prototype the same kind of rhythm loop on iPad with hyperPad's visual Behaviors:


1. **Build one play Scene.** Add four target Objects near one edge of the screen and a UI label for the score and misses.
2. **Create one note Object.** Give it a` direction` Attribute and send it toward its target at a steady speed. See[Object Attributes](https://www.hyperpad.com/documentation/object-attributes) .
3. **Read the player's input.** Use[Started Touching](https://www.hyperpad.com/documentation/started-touching) on four on-screen controls, and an[If](https://www.hyperpad.com/documentation/if) Behavior to check whether the note in the hit zone matches.
4. **Judge the timing.** A small hit zone around each target makes timing stricter. A bigger zone is more forgiving.
5. **Add feedback.** On a hit, remove the note, add to the score, and flash the target. On a miss, update the miss counter.
6. **Add music last.** Trigger a short loop with[Play Music](https://www.hyperpad.com/documentation/play-music) once the timing feels fair.


This makes a new game of your own. It doesn't edit the official FNF game, and it doesn't give permission to reuse FNF characters, music, or art. Use your own characters, songs, Graphics, and rules.


For a full build plan, follow the[FNF mod-style game guide for iPad](https://www.hyperpad.com/blog/how-to-make-a-friday-night-funkin-mod-on-ipad-mobile-no-code-guide) .
